name: Generic Sensor Evaluation Lab
description: Deterministic synthetic reference profile for the MultiSens v0.4/v0.5 requirement-coverage and condition-exploration workflow. SYNTHETIC DATA - demonstrates functionality only, not a claim about real sensor performance. See examples/profiles/README.md.

requirements.name: Day baseline
requirements.description: Baseline presence accuracy in daylight with a clear (unoccluded) view.

requirements.name: Night baseline
requirements.description: Baseline presence accuracy at night with a clear (unoccluded) view.

requirements.name: Day, partial occlusion
requirements.description: Presence accuracy in daylight with partial occlusion of the sensor's view.

requirements.name: Night, partial occlusion
requirements.description: Presence accuracy at night with partial occlusion of the sensor's view - the hardest single-dimension case in this demo.

requirements.name: Strict day accuracy
requirements.description: A stricter accuracy bar under the same daylight/clear-view conditions as the Baseline Detection group - demonstrates that the same evidence can satisfy one requirement and fail another; acceptance is requirement-specific, not a property of the configuration alone.

requirements.name: Strict night accuracy
requirements.description: A stricter accuracy bar under the same night/clear-view conditions as the Baseline Detection group.

requirements.name: Day, rain
requirements.description: Presence accuracy in daylight with a clear (unoccluded) view, under rain - same acceptance bar as the day baseline, so a pass/fail difference is attributable to weather alone, not a stricter threshold.

requirements.name: Night, rain
requirements.description: Presence accuracy at night with a clear (unoccluded) view, under rain - same acceptance bar as the night baseline. Thermal specifically fails this one where it passes the night baseline, demonstrating that a condition dimension can flip an outcome, not just shift a number.
